A LITTLE PHILOSOPHY

Powerful agents.
Informed humans.

01 /

Put context where decisions happen.

An environment under a command. An impact preview at approval. An action map beside your work.

02 /

Keep the boundaries clear.

env-badge, blast-radius, and footprint provide visibility. They don’t allow or block commands, and their parsers have limits. A missing indicator doesn’t mean an action is safe.

03 /

Make what you learn yours.

2brain stores knowledge in Markdown and JSONL in a Git repository. Read it, inspect it, and carry it into your next session.

Claude Code plugin questions.

Can I install Claude Code plugins independently?

Yes. Each plugin has its own repository and can be installed independently. Start with the gap in your workflow that matters most.

Do these plugins prevent dangerous commands?

No. env-badge, blast-radius, and footprint are display tools, not security gates. Keep using Claude Code’s permission controls. The parsers cannot see every action inside scripts, wrappers, or other tools.

How do I install these Claude Code plugins?

Add the safeinfra/claude-marketplace marketplace, then install the plugin you need using the commands in the installation section above. The three display plugins use Claude Code function hooks. Enable them as described in each README. footprint is public on GitHub. 2brain requires repository access. For 2brain, follow its installer guide to set up the knowledge directory and optional maintenance jobs.

Which plugins help with AWS and Kubernetes workflows?

claude-env-badge shows AWS profiles and Kubernetes contexts under Bash commands. claude-footprint maps parsed AWS, Kubernetes, and supported MCP activity so you can see scope, action class, and reported outcomes.

How does persistent memory work across Claude Code sessions?

Yes. 2brain captures session lessons in a plain-text wiki and recalls relevant knowledge in future Claude Code and Codex sessions. Its repository is private, and access is required to install it.

Which Claude Code plugin previews rm -rf deletion impact?

claude-blast-radius shows file counts, total size, and files not tracked by Git before you approve supported Bash deletion commands. Its impact preview helps you review destructive commands; Claude Code still handles permission decisions.

Does claude-footprint track MCP tool calls?

claude-footprint maps supported Model Context Protocol (MCP) activity alongside parsed AWS and Kubernetes commands. It displays scope, action class, and reported outcomes. Coverage depends on the supported parsers; it does not observe every tool or action.

How can these plugins help a DevOps workflow?

Use env-badge to see the AWS profile or Kubernetes context during cloud infrastructure work, blast-radius to review file deletion impact, footprint to inspect agent activity, and 2brain to recall lessons from earlier sessions. Install each plugin through the Safe Infra Claude Code plugin marketplace.
